name: The Politics of AI
blurb:
This hub records what can be checked and leaves motive to the reader. A lobbying filing shows that lobbying happened on an issue, not what was argued. A contribution shown beside a vote is placed there for comparison, not as a claim that one caused the other.

Sections open as their data is complete enough to be useful. Lobbying on AI is first. Money beside votes, bills and outcomes by issue, and the preemption watch follow as the Congress and Federal Election Commission data finish loading.
summary: Who in government is doing what about AI, shown through the public record: lobbying filed on AI, the bills and votes in Congress, the money from AI company committees, and the federal effort to override state AI laws. Every entry cites the filing, vote or record it rests on.

children.desc: 3630 Lobbying Disclosure Act filings posted between 2023-01-09 and 2026-09-15 report lobbying the federal government on artificial intelligence or machine learning, for 918 clients through 585 registrants. The 150 clients with the most filings are listed below, each linked to its latest filing on lda.gov.
